articles.headline: INSTANTANEOUS ROUND-UP VIEWS.
articles.text:
INSTANTANEOUS ROUND-UP VIEWS.

We have remaining a few sets of Huffmann's instantaneous round-up views, representing the most interesting events of the range cattle industry. There are thirty-six well-executed photographs in the series, making an extremely interesting and realistic panorama of cowboy life. We will sell the complete set for $5 or,

THE COW BOY A YEAR AND THE SET, $6

This offer will probably be recalled soon, but the bargain can now be secured by calling on or addressing
THE BAD LANDS COW BOY,
Medora, Dak.
articles.summary: The Cow Boy offers its remaining sets of Huffman's thirty-six round-up photographs for $5, or $6 with a year's subscription.

articles.text: Further shocks of earth-quake were felt in Charleston Tuesday night, which had the effect of terrorizing the already frightened inhabitants, although but little additional damage was done.
articles.summary: Further earthquake shocks struck Charleston Tuesday night, with little additional damage.

articles.text: The number of acres of public land disposed of in Dakota this year is 3,075,085; nearly as much as Iowa, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Montana, Oregon, Washington and Wyoming put together.
articles.summary: Dakota disposed of 3,075,085 acres of public land this year.

articles.text: We are just in receipt from J. S. Collins & Co., of one of the new "Letter Sheet Envelopes," the first we have seen. The new departure will be handy in many ways and doubtless extensively used.
articles.summary: The Cow Boy received one of the new letter-sheet envelopes from J. S. Collins & Co.

articles.text: In the base-ball contest for the championship of the National League, the Chicagos have a clear lead of seven games over the Detroits, who stand second, while the New Yorks are a bad third. There seems no reason to doubt that the season will be closed in this order by the three leaders.
articles.summary: Chicago leads the National League by seven games over Detroit.

articles.text: Although the Mandan Pioneer was very quick to criticize the COW BOY'S action in proposing a candidate for the Legislature; in fact, criticized the idea of our making a choice before we had made one, it has not had the back-bone to commend any candidate to the public. We are at a loss to understand the Pioneer's course, as the very least it could do would be to name the candidates and praise or condemn them alike. Instead of this, it is as mum as an oyster on the subject.
articles.summary: The Cow Boy chides the Mandan Pioneer for criticizing its legislative endorsement while naming no candidate itself.

articles.text: The Republican primary convention of Billings county, made a good choice in its delegates to the Bismarck convention. Neither of them was present at the convention, but they will fully represent Billings county's sentiments at the convention. They are not instructed, but have hitherto expressed decided preferences for Mr. Lyon of Mandan. They will doubtless stick to their choice as long as there is any chance for success, which at present seems a good one.
articles.summary: The Cow Boy approves the Billings county delegates to the Bismarck convention, who favor Mr. Lyon of Mandan.

articles.text: A report is going the rounds that Stark county was depending on Billings county's delegation, for support at the Bismarck convention. We doubt if this is well-founded, as no effort whatever has been made by Stark county to enlist aid from here. We do not know even that Stark county has a pronounced candidate and even if it had, there is no chance for his nomination. It is far better to unite on some good man who will have a good fighting chance for the nomination.
articles.summary: The Cow Boy doubts a report that Stark county counted on Billings county's delegation at Bismarck.

articles.text: The Republican congressional convention, now in session at Yankton will probably not get to balloting before to-morrow as there are a number of contests to be settled. Gifford's friends claim that he will be nominated on the first ballot, while the opposition claim that he will go into the convention with only 190 votes to 210 in opposition and sixty-four doubtful and contested. The opposition claim that there is a good chance of nominating Gen'l. Allen of Fargo or Judge Palmer of Sioux Falls, with chances in favor of the latter.
articles.summary: The Republican congressional convention at Yankton is expected to ballot tomorrow; Gifford, Allen and Palmer are named.

articles.text: We are in receipt of a "chromio" from Pozzoni's Complexion Powder Co., that in the hints given us as the basis of a laudatory article, is described as "the most expensive and artistic ever published. An ornament to the parlor or the office of the most fastidious." We don't pretend to be a judge of high art, which may account for the fact that we at first took it for a picture of a dashing equestrienne on a circus poster. We morever seriously doubt if a complexion powder company will make its everlasting fortune in the cow country. It is positively affecting to imagine a stalwart puncher in his boudoir, powdering his face in front of his full-length, plate glass mirror, as a protection against the injurious effect on his countenance of the delicate blizzard or the coy chinook. Oh yes, Mr. Pozzoni, bring out a hay rack full and sell it to the boys by the barrel.
articles.summary: The Cow Boy pokes fun at a promotional chromo from Pozzoni's Complexion Powder Co.

articles.headline: Republican Convention.
articles.text:
Republican Convention.

At a Republican caucus, held in the Court House in Medora, Monday evening Sept. 20, 1886, J. C. Fisher was elected chairman and J. C. Williamson, secretary.

The meeting proceeded at once to the nomination of delegates to the convention at Bismarck, Oct. 3.

The names of J. A. Ferris, D. W. Williams and F. A. Willard were successively proposed and the nominees declined.

The names of Howard Eaton and G. G. Bond being presented they were elected by acclamation.

A resolution proposed by D. W. Williams to the effect that a Stark county man should be supported in the convention at Bismarck, was lost.

J. C. WILLIAMSON,
Secretary.
articles.summary: Minutes of the Medora Republican caucus of Sept. 20, which elected Howard Eaton and G. G. Bond delegates to the Bismarck convention.

articles.text: St. Paul has made an enviable reputation this season as a stock market for small outfits, sales of from two to six cars there bringing prices from fifty cents to a dollar a hundred higher not than in Chicago. It would be a great relief to the cowmen of the northwest if a market could be established there even as large as those at Kansas City or even Omaha. It would at all times act as a kind of check on any attempt to bear the Chicago market and create a healthy competition very beneficial to our cattle industry. We are as much in the dark as ever, though, how yards can be established at St. Paul that will take the whole northwestern output of cattle. The market is too firmly established in Chicago.
articles.summary: The Cow Boy notes St. Paul's strong prices for small cattle shipments this season but doubts it can replace Chicago.

articles.text: The 777 wagons arrived at Mingusville yesterday and the outfit will load a train to-morrow.
articles.summary: The 777 outfit's wagons reached Mingusville to load a cattle train.

articles.text: M. C. Conners passed through Medora Friday morning, following the first of five trains of his cattle shipped from Mingusville. He said he would feed as long as he could buy hay, before he sold on a low market.
articles.summary: M. C. Conners followed the first of five trainloads of his cattle shipped from Mingusville.

articles.text: After many inquiries, we learn that the standard rule for determining the blood of an animal is to add the fractions of the parents and divide by two. For instance, five-eighths and three-eighths Shorthorn parents would produce a half-blood Shorthorn calf.
articles.summary: Explains the rule for figuring an animal's fraction of blood.

articles.text: Ex-Senator Dorsey of New Mexico, has a team that he recently drove to a carriage containing three persons, twenty-eight miles in two hours. There were rough places in the road also, that frequently compelled the horses to walk.
articles.summary: Ex-Senator Dorsey drove a team 28 miles in two hours.

articles.text: Gregor Lang returned last Thursday evening from St. Paul, where he sold his cattle. The steers brought $3.60 and a few dry cows, $2.90. This price was about forty cents higher than the Chicago market, netting at least seventy-five cents per hundred more than if they had been taken through.
articles.summary: Gregor Lang sold his cattle at St. Paul, steers bringing $3.60.

articles.text: From all northern ranges comes the report that cattle were never in better condition in spite of the drougth. We dislike to stand against almost the unanimous voice of the northwestern range press, but It is impossible to truthfully say that cattle are better than in fair condition. They are not in poor condition but are poorer than far several years in spite of the excellent Bad Lands ranges.
articles.summary: The Cow Boy disputes reports of excellent cattle condition, calling them only fair after the drought.

articles.text: Henry Boice has shipped from Townsend, Montana, about 400 head of mares and colts. They will be put on the Beaver creek range of the 777 outfit, and will, in the future, furnish all the cow-horses necessary for the range work of the company. This is a move which could be profitably imitated by almost every outfit in the country. Cow-horses in the north are too high and it will pay much better to raise them than to buy at $50 to $70 each. Many outfits have gone into the business of raising heavy draft and work horses, but no new ones are raising cow-horses. Unless measures like the above are extensively taken, the price of cow-horses will constantly rise.
articles.summary: Henry Boice shipped about 400 mares and colts from Townsend, Montana, to the 777's Beaver creek range to raise cow-horses.

articles.text: From articles in our stock exchanges, we think that 30,000 head is a moderate estimate of the number of cattle sent to the Northwest Territory this summer. All seem agreed that the range is not better there and the only advantage is that a man controls his own range and can do as he pleases with it. The exodus shows pretty clearly that the Montana ranges are pretty well stocked, as the expense of moving is considerable and the benefits to be derived would not be sufficient to justify the move, if there was perfect safety in staying on the old ranges. The 30,000 head can then be considered as the surplus of the Montana ranges, which has, so to speak, slopped over into Canada.
articles.summary: About 30,000 head of cattle were moved to the Canadian Northwest Territory this summer, a sign Montana ranges are well stocked.

articles.headline: A Rise Inevitable.
articles.text:
A Rise Inevitable.

It has become plain to every student of statistics that no class of meat-producing animals, except possibly the hog, can be increased with a rapidity sufficient to meet the increasing demand for it. There is not only the increase of population to be met but there is an astonishing increase of meat consumption in all the countries of the world. In this country in 1850 there were [814?] cattle to the 1,000 population. Now there are only 772 to the 1,000 population. This decrease has certainly occured during the period of greatest prosperity in cattle raising on a large scale—when the free grasses on the public lands, the vast sums of willing capital, and the skill and energy of the ranchmen and feeders all favored to the highest degree a rate of production above the average of any other period. The total population of the United States doubles every twenty-five years, but east of the Mississippi the increase of cattle has been less than one-third as great. The annual increase of the population of the entire country is to the annual increase of stock as 2¾ to 1½ per cent., or an excess of increase of population over increase of stock of over 55 per cent.

It is easy to see from the above data that our own requirements are more than a match for our own production under even the most favorable conditions. We cannot hasten breeding operations to any appreciable degree but must content ourselves with about a slow 50 per cent. annual increase or a calf for every two she cattle in the land. But our home demand is not the sole absorber of our products. The British population is increasing at the rate of 1,000 per day, which, at the present rate of consumption, would require an increase of 40,000,000 pounds per annum!

In 1840 the consumption of meat in Great Britain per capita was 61 lbs; in 1850 it was 67 lbs; in 1860, 77 lbs; in 1870, 88 lbs; in 1875, 96 lbs, and in 1882, 109 lbs. per annum. Of this 109 lbs, 56 lbs. was beef. From 1840 to 1850 the increase was only 6 lbs. per capita while it was 21 lbs or 3½ times as great from 1870 to 1882, and the population increased in the latter period [2½?] times as fast as during the former. In France the consumption of beef increased from 19 lbs per capita in 1840 to 40 lbs in 1880 There is a felt deficiency in the beef supply throughout Europe. There during twenty-five years previous to 1880, the cattle had increased only 10 per cent., but the population increased 22 per cent. The United States citizens requires 150 lbs of meat per annum.

The demand for our meat products is not only increasing, but this increase is a growing and permanent one. Can it be met? Probably not. Already we lack in numbers of productive stock and from the west the great source of supply—for the last two years has come to us the complaint of overstocking. At first this was received as the cry of some alarmist who was seeking to frighten some timid people into withdrawing from the cattle business and to deter others from entering upon it, but now, after two consecutive winters and one summer of heavy losses it begins to be seen that really many of the ranches are overstocked. There can be no expansion, therefore, in that direction. But an increase can be made in the producing areas by utilizing some of our mountain regions, in dividing some of the large herds and grazing the subdivisions on areas neglected to the present on account of their smallness, and an increase, and possibly the largest increase in our beef feeding capacity, can be made in the farm districts of the country. Our farmers are not producing 50 per cent. of the cattle food that they should and the combined causes of loss probably leave not over 50 per cent. of the entire products to be actually utilized for conversion into meat, but of these cattlemen will take advantage but slowly because in the first the matter will be considered as a utilization of waste places and the second involves a new and improved system of agriculture and enlarged knowledge of the science of feeding that will require time to meet. While production halts at obstacles and speculates as to the probabilities the pace of demand is neither turned nor retarded. It is inexorable and meat must be forthcoming cheaply if possible, but be the price what it may, meat must come. Barring war prices meat is higher now than ever, except possibly during some short period when it has been unwarrantably "boomed," and is sure to continue on its upward tendency. The cattleman has as bright a day before him as anyone. He may not realize during the next six months or even the next twelve, though it is not impossible that he should at once, but let him stay with his herds, the good time cannot fail him. Breeders are not pushing Angus, Galloways, Herefords, Shorthorns, etc., as if the time had [come?] to discard anything so meritorious as even the poorest breed in the list. Instead of advising the pushing out of either breed the Record will urge the pushing of all of them forward to the point of perfection.—[Kansas City L. S. Indicator.
articles.summary: Reprinted from the Kansas City Live Stock Indicator: growing meat demand at home and in Europe makes a rise in cattle prices inevitable.

articles.summary: Northern Pacific stock quotations.

articles.text: The Co. has sold about 1,500 hides to Allen & Sons of Kenosha, Wis.
articles.summary: "The Co." sold about 1,500 hides to Allen & Sons of Kenosha.

articles.text: G. G. Cooper, a former operator here, is now pounding the key for the Western Union in St. Paul.
articles.summary: Former Medora telegraph operator G. G. Cooper now works for Western Union in St. Paul.

articles.text: Howard Eaton shipped the last of his tame buffalo to B. J. VanVleck of Mandan, this morning.
articles.summary: Howard Eaton shipped the last of his tame buffalo to B. J. VanVleck of Mandan.

articles.text: D. K. Wade and sister will start the first of the week for California where they will spend the winter.
articles.summary: D. K. Wade and his sister will leave to winter in California.

articles.text: John Pohl strained himself in some way Saturday and was taken to the Bismarck hospital for treatment.
articles.summary: John Pohl was injured and taken to the Bismarck hospital.

articles.text: T. R. Selmes of Mandan, is expected here soon, to take a hunt with his stag-hounds after deer and antelope.
articles.summary: T. R. Selmes of Mandan is expected to hunt deer and antelope with staghounds.

articles.text: Too late for last issue, we learned that E. Elmer and wife are rejoicing over the appearance of a brand-new girl baby.
articles.summary: E. Elmer and his wife had a baby girl.

articles.text: The Democrats didn't "convensh" to any material extent and the Aberdeen convention will be short two delegates from Billings county.
articles.summary: Billings county will be two delegates short at the Democratic convention in Aberdeen.

articles.text: The OX round-up will probably pass through Medora to-morrow or Saturday. This will be the last beef round-up of the season on the river.
articles.summary: The OX beef round-up, the season's last on the river, is expected through Medora.

articles.text: Tom. Matthews, at present stock inspector at Glendive, has received the Democratic nomination for sheriff of Dawson county, Montana.
articles.summary: Glendive stock inspector Tom Matthews was nominated for Dawson county sheriff by the Democrats.

articles.text: Frank Foster has gone to Chicago, where he will meet the Marquis. They will then go to Kansas City to look up a plant where beef can be killed all winter.
articles.summary: Frank Foster went to Chicago to meet the Marquis; they will seek a winter beef-killing plant at Kansas City.

articles.text: Prairie chickens are getting wild and except for the bag of thirty-four killed by Wm. Van Driesche and Frank Foster in two hours, no large killings have been made.
articles.summary: Van Driesche and Foster killed 34 prairie chickens in two hours.

articles.text: P. S. Bemis who has been "cow-punching" on the river for over a year, will start Sunday for Arizona. He will run a wagon in a large outfit there owned by some of his New York friends.
articles.summary: P. S. Bemis leaves Sunday to run a wagon for an Arizona outfit.

articles.text: Fred Willard wants it gently insinuated that the "cooler" is in running order now and that the price of custard pies may come higher. He adds that he would'nt care so much if the pie plates were returned.
articles.summary: Fred Willard's "cooler" is running and he asks for his pie plates back.

articles.text: C. L. McGee, wife and sister, who have been visiting at the Logging Camp and at Howard and Charlie Eaton's ranches, will start Sunday for their home in Pittsburgh. Mr. McGee is interested in the SO brand.
articles.summary: C. L. McGee of Pittsburgh, interested in the SO brand, ends a visit to the Eaton ranches.

articles.text: Although it is a rather malodorous subject to bring up, we would like to inquire for an explanation of the large number of skunks appearing this year. From the Glendive papers we learn that they are unusually numerous there also.
articles.summary: Skunks are unusually numerous around Medora and Glendive this year.

articles.text: J. N. Maxwell, well-remembered as rail-road agent here, is now running as messenger for the American express Co., on the Manitoba road, between St. Paul and Fargo. His wife is visiting "Max's" parents at Port Byron, Ill.
articles.summary: Former Medora railroad agent J. N. Maxwell is now an express messenger on the Manitoba road.

articles.text: A wreck occurred at Black River Falls, Wis., yesterday, in which forty head of cattle were killed and many more injured. The cattle are thought to have been shipped from Mingusville, but it is not as yet known who is the owner.
articles.summary: A wreck at Black River Falls, Wis., killed forty cattle believed shipped from Mingusville.

articles.text: As an illustration of the harm done by hail and drought this summer it is only necessary to state that but eighty-one bushels of oats were threshed in the farms tributary to South Heart. Last year's figures are not obtainable but there were thousands of bushels.
articles.summary: Hail and drought left only 81 bushels of oats threshed around South Heart.

articles.text: It is a fact that seems not to be well-known that the bite of a skunk is as dangerous as that of a mad dog. Our exchanges have lately mentioned several cases of persons dying from hydrophobia who have been bitten by skunks. In view of this fact they should be killed as relentlessly as rattlesnakes.
articles.summary: The Cow Boy warns that skunk bites can cause hydrophobia.

articles.text: The jail cells have been completed at the Court house and we hope will remain in their present empty state for a long time. They are fire-proof but "lack lots" of being warm as there is no way of heating them except perhaps by setting the Court house on fire. Boarders must remember to bring their overcoats with them this winter or they may have a wooden one made for them at the county's expense.
articles.summary: The jail cells at the Medora court house are completed.

articles.text: Theodore Roosevelt and W. H. Merrifield returned Saturday from the Bull river mountains, where they have been hunting for the past month. The trip was undertaken for the purpose of killing a white goat. The hunters were completely successful, killing three of this rare kind of game. Their coat is composed of a thick inner layer of wool, through which protrudes a longer growth of a hairy fur, both being snow-white. The horns are about a foot long, taper gracefully to a sharp point and curve backward like those of an ibex.
articles.summary: Theodore Roosevelt and W. H. Merrifield returned from a month's hunt in the Bull river mountains with three white goats.

Brand: Little Missouri Horse Company, [illegible] Tarbell, M'n'g'r, Medora, Dak. — range Davis creek and Little Missouri river
Brand: W. N. Thompson & Co., Wm. Dantz, Manager, P.O. Medora, Billings Co., Dak.

events.date_basis: "Saturday" before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Theodore Roosevelt and Merrifield return from white-goat hunt
events.summary: Theodore Roosevelt and W. H. Merrifield returned from a month's hunt in the Bull river mountains, where they killed three white goats, the object of the trip.
events.excerpt: Theodore Roosevelt and W. H. Merrifield returned Saturday from the Bull river mountains, where they have been hunting for the past month.

events.date_basis: Dated in text: "Monday evening Sept. 20, 1886"
events.title: Medora Republican caucus elects Eaton and Bond as delegates
events.summary: A Republican caucus at the Medora court house, with J. C. Fisher chairing, elected Howard Eaton and G. G. Bond delegates to the Bismarck convention of Oct. 3 after Ferris, Williams and Willard declined. A resolution to back a Stark county man failed.
events.excerpt: The names of Howard Eaton and G. G. Bond being presented they were elected by acclamation.

events.date_basis: Convention date given in text: "Bismarck, Oct. 3"
events.title: Bismarck Republican convention scheduled
events.summary: Billings county's delegates are to attend the Republican convention at Bismarck on Oct. 3, where they favor Mr. Lyon of Mandan.
events.excerpt: They are not instructed, but have hitherto expressed decided preferences for Mr. Lyon of Mandan.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Cow Boy chides Mandan Pioneer over legislative candidates
events.summary: The Cow Boy said the Mandan Pioneer had criticized its endorsement of a legislative candidate but had not named or commended any candidate itself.
events.excerpt: it is as mum as an oyster on the subject.

events.date_basis: "yesterday" before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: 777 wagons arrive at Mingusville to ship cattle
events.summary: The 777 outfit's wagons arrived at Mingusville, and the outfit was to load a train the next day.
events.excerpt: The 777 wagons arrived at Mingusville yesterday and the outfit will load a train to-morrow.

events.date_basis: "Friday" before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: M. C. Conners ships five trains of cattle from Mingusville
events.summary: M. C. Conners passed through Medora following the first of five trains of his cattle shipped from Mingusville; he said he would feed as long as he could buy hay rather than sell on a low market.
events.excerpt: M. C. Conners passed through Medora Friday morning, following the first of five trains of his cattle shipped from Mingusville.

events.date_basis: "last Thursday" before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Gregor Lang returns from selling cattle at St. Paul
events.summary: Gregor Lang returned from St. Paul, where his steers brought $3.60 and some dry cows $2.90, about forty cents above the Chicago market.
events.excerpt: Gregor Lang returned last Thursday evening from St. Paul, where he sold his cattle.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Cattle on Bad Lands ranges only in fair condition after drought
events.summary: The Cow Boy disputed the range press's reports, saying cattle were in only fair condition and poorer than for several years, in spite of good Bad Lands ranges.
events.excerpt: It is impossible to truthfully say that cattle are better than in fair condition.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Henry Boice ships 400 mares and colts to 777 range
events.summary: Henry Boice shipped about 400 mares and colts from Townsend, Montana, for the 777 outfit's Beaver creek range, to raise all the company's cow-horses.
events.excerpt: Henry Boice has shipped from Townsend, Montana, about 400 head of mares and colts.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Richardton double R herd offered for sale
events.summary: The Richardton (double R) herd of Hereford bulls, cows and half-Hereford young stock was advertised for sale through agent Adolph Nordberg.
events.excerpt: The Richardton (double R) herd, consisting of:

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Red roan horse strays from Garner Creek Horse Ranch
events.summary: J. A. VanEeghen advertised for a red roan horse, branded C bar and VE, that strayed from the Garner Creek Horse Ranch.
events.excerpt: One red roan horse, branded C bar on left shoulder and VE connected on left hip.

events.date_basis: "this summer" per issue of Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: About 30,000 cattle moved to the Canadian Northwest this summer
events.summary: The Cow Boy estimated that 30,000 head of cattle were sent to the Northwest Territory this summer, the surplus of Montana's well-stocked ranges.
events.excerpt: 30,000 head is a moderate estimate of the number of cattle sent to the Northwest Territory this summer.

events.date_basis: "Monday" before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Railroad pay-wagon passes through Medora
events.summary: The railroad pay-wagon came through Monday.
events.excerpt: The pay-wagon came through Monday.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: "The Co." sells 1,500 hides to Kenosha firm
events.summary: The Co. sold about 1,500 hides to Allen & Sons of Kenosha, Wisconsin.
events.excerpt: The Co. has sold about 1,500 hides to Allen & Sons of Kenosha, Wis.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Former Medora operator G. G. Cooper joins Western Union in St. Paul
events.summary: G. G. Cooper, formerly the telegraph operator at Medora, is now working for Western Union in St. Paul.
events.excerpt: G. G. Cooper, a former operator here, is now pounding the key for the Western Union in St. Paul.

events.date_basis: "this morning" in issue of Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Howard Eaton ships last of his tame buffalo to Mandan
events.summary: Howard Eaton shipped the last of his tame buffalo to B. J. VanVleck of Mandan.
events.excerpt: Howard Eaton shipped the last of his tame buffalo to B. J. VanVleck of Mandan, this morning.

events.date_basis: "the first of the week" after Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: D. K. Wade and sister leave to winter in California
events.summary: D. K. Wade and his sister plan to leave early in the week for California, where they will spend the winter.
events.excerpt: D. K. Wade and sister will start the first of the week for California where they will spend the winter.

events.date_basis: "Saturday" before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: John Pohl injured and taken to Bismarck hospital
events.summary: John Pohl strained himself and was taken to the Bismarck hospital for treatment.
events.excerpt: John Pohl strained himself in some way Saturday and was taken to the Bismarck hospital for treatment.

events.date_basis: "expected here soon" per issue of Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: T. R. Selmes expected for staghound hunt
events.summary: T. R. Selmes of Mandan was expected soon at Medora to hunt deer and antelope with his staghounds.
events.excerpt: T. R. Selmes of Mandan, is expected here soon, to take a hunt with his stag-hounds after deer and antelope.

events.date_basis: "Too late for last issue" (Thu 16 Sep 1886); birth on or before about that date
events.title: Baby girl born to E. Elmer and wife
events.summary: E. Elmer and his wife had a baby girl, news that came too late for the previous issue.
events.excerpt: E. Elmer and wife are rejoicing over the appearance of a brand-new girl baby.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Billings county Democrats fail to fill Aberdeen delegation
events.summary: The Democrats held no real convention, and Billings county will be two delegates short at the Aberdeen convention.
events.excerpt: the Aberdeen convention will be short two delegates from Billings county.

events.date_basis: "to-morrow or Saturday" after Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: OX beef round-up expected through Medora
events.summary: The OX round-up, the last beef round-up of the season on the river, was expected to pass through Medora.
events.excerpt: The OX round-up will probably pass through Medora to-morrow or Saturday.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Tom Matthews nominated for sheriff of Dawson county
events.summary: Tom Matthews, stock inspector at Glendive, received the Democratic nomination for sheriff of Dawson county, Montana.
events.excerpt: has received the Democratic nomination for sheriff of Dawson county, Montana.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Frank Foster goes to Chicago to meet the Marquis
events.summary: Frank Foster went to Chicago to meet the Marquis de Morès; the two were then to go to Kansas City to look for a plant where beef could be killed all winter.
events.excerpt: Frank Foster has gone to Chicago, where he will meet the Marquis.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Van Driesche and Foster bag 34 prairie chickens
events.summary: Prairie chickens were getting wild, but Wm. Van Driesche and Frank Foster killed thirty-four in two hours.
events.excerpt: the bag of thirty-four killed by Wm. Van Driesche and Frank Foster in two hours

events.date_basis: "Sunday" after Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: P. S. Bemis leaves for Arizona
events.summary: P. S. Bemis, who had been cow-punching on the river for over a year, planned to leave for Arizona to run a wagon for an outfit owned by New York friends.
events.excerpt: will start Sunday for Arizona.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Fred Willard's "cooler" in running order
events.summary: Fred Willard announced that his "cooler" was running and that the price of custard pies might rise, and asked for his pie plates back.
events.excerpt: the "cooler" is in running order now

events.date_basis: "Sunday" after Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: C. L. McGee party ends visit to Eaton ranches
events.summary: C. L. McGee, his wife and sister, who had visited the Logging Camp and Howard and Charlie Eaton's ranches, were to leave for Pittsburgh. McGee is interested in the SO brand.
events.excerpt: will start Sunday for their home in Pittsburgh.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Skunks unusually numerous
events.summary: The Cow Boy noted a large number of skunks this year, also reported at Glendive, and warned that skunk bites could cause hydrophobia.
events.excerpt: the large number of skunks appearing this year

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Former agent J. N. Maxwell now an express messenger
events.summary: J. N. Maxwell, formerly railroad agent at Medora, is now an American Express messenger on the Manitoba road between St. Paul and Fargo.
events.excerpt: J. N. Maxwell, well-remembered as rail-road agent here

events.date_basis: "yesterday" before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Wreck kills forty head of cattle believed shipped from Mingusville
events.summary: A wreck at Black River Falls, Wisconsin, killed forty head of cattle and injured many more; the cattle were thought to have been shipped from Mingusville.
events.excerpt: A wreck occurred at Black River Falls, Wis., yesterday, in which forty head of cattle were killed

events.date_basis: "this summer" per issue of Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Hail and drought ruin South Heart oat crop
events.summary: Hail and drought left only eighty-one bushels of oats threshed on farms around South Heart, against thousands the year before.
events.excerpt: but eighty-one bushels of oats were threshed in the farms tributary to South Heart.

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Jail cells completed at Medora court house
events.summary: The jail cells at the court house were completed; the Cow Boy joked they could be heated only by setting the court house on fire.
events.excerpt: The jail cells have been completed at the Court house

events.date_basis: No date given; week before Thu 23 Sep 1886
events.title: Packard closes out Studebaker wagon stock
events.summary: A. T. Packard offered his remaining Studebaker wagons for cash below wholesale factory rates to close out the stock.
events.excerpt: To close out the stock of Studebaker wagons now on hand
